benchmark: T25 driver-level pipe vs native-DLL head-to-head
method: wrapper-level transport overhead, both lanes with FAKE responders (same harness as the 44x pipe-vs-oneshot bench); isolates the transport boundary cost, apples-to-apples

summary.verdict: At the driver/wrapper level the pipe lane is at parity or marginally CHEAPER than the in-process ExternalObject DLL boundary (pipe 0.071-0.078ms vs DLL 0.084-0.141ms; ratio 0.55-0.87x). Both are sub-0.15ms — the transport boundary overhead is negligible and roughly equal; the real-world comparison is dominated by network/WinHTTP latency, not the transport selection.
